## Architecture map — what the engine actually does

This is a 2-minute orientation for whoever picks up S2-B (W10). It's what I had to reconstruct by reading [engine.py](../approval-api/app/crud/engine.py) — none of this is documented elsewhere.

### State vocabulary (HARDCODED throughout the engine)

The approval engine reads + writes `doc.status` as a plain string with this fixed set of values:

```
draft  →  submitted  →  in_review  →  approved
                  ↘  returned  (→  back to submitted on resubmit)
                  ↘  rejected
                  ↘  cancelled
                  ↘  processed   (PA only, after pay)
```

This is **not negotiable per-doc-type**. It's baked into `execute_action()` at engine.py:553–675:

```python
if act == "submit":
    if doc.status not in meta["valid_submit"]:  # meta CAN constrain entry states
        raise ValueError(...)
    doc.status = "submitted"                    # but the WRITE values are hardcoded
    ...
elif act == "approve":
    ...
    if next_step < len(workflow):
        doc.status = "in_review"
    else:
        doc.status = "approved"
        ...
```

Every existing doc (PR, PO, PA, EXP, MIL, TRV, CFM, BudgetPlan) has its `status` column as a free `String` with these exact values. The engine assumes write-access to that string field with that vocabulary.

### Per-doc-type plug-in surface (`_DOC_META[doc_type]`)

What each new doc_type contributes:

```python
{
    "model":        ORMClass,       # the engine SELECTs by id from this table
    "number_attr":  "field_name",   # → goes into Task.document_number (40-char string)
    "amount_attr":  "field_name",   # → Task.amount (Decimal | None)
    "vendor_attr":  "field_name",   # → Task.vendor (str | None)
    "task_approve": "type_string",  # → Task.type when creating an approval task
    "task_revise":  "type_string",  # → Task.type when creating a revise task
    "valid_submit":  (states, ...), # gating predicates only — write value is hardcoded
    "valid_approve": (states, ...),
    "valid_return":  (states, ...),
    "valid_cancel":  (states, ...),
}
```

Note `_DOC_META` does NOT include:
- A status WRITE-value override → that's hardcoded.
- A `title_attr` → engine reads `doc.title` directly (line 345: `title=f"Approve {doc_type.upper()}: {doc_number} — {doc.title}"`).
- A `status_attr` → engine reads `doc.status` directly.

### Task creation signature

When the engine creates a Task row ([engine.py:298–349](../approval-api/app/crud/engine.py)):

```python
db.add(Task(
    type=meta["task_approve"],         # e.g. "approve_vms_visit"
    priority="normal",
    document_type=doc_type,            # "vms_visit" — must fit String(10)
    document_id=doc.id,                # UUID
    document_number=doc_number,        # getattr(doc, meta["number_attr"])
    assigned_role=assigned_role,
    assigned_user_id=assigned_user_id, # nullable; falls back to role-broadcast
    title=f"Approve {doc_type.upper()}: {doc_number} — {doc.title}",
    description=...,
    amount=getattr(doc, meta["amount_attr"]),
    vendor=getattr(doc, meta["vendor_attr"], None),
))
```

Assignment logic is hardcoded per role string:

```python
if role == "dept_manager":
    assigned_user_id = await _get_dept_manager_id(db, doc.created_by)
elif role == "gm_or_opm":
    assigned_role, assigned_user_id = await _resolve_gm_or_opm(db, doc.created_by, rm, dept_gm_opm)
# else: assigned_user_id stays None → role-broadcast via assigned_role
```

To wire `quality_manager`, we need to add another `elif` branch here.

### Portal Task Inbox — how tasks reach the user

Portal's `useEpmsTasks` calls **epms-api** `GET /api/v1/tasks` ([portal/src/pages/PortalHome.tsx:77–82](../portal/src/pages/PortalHome.tsx#L77-L82)). epms-api's `task_crud.get_for_role` ([epms-api/app/crud/task.py:142–173](../epms-api/app/crud/task.py#L142-L173)) returns tasks matching:

```sql
(assigned_user_id IS NULL AND assigned_role IN <user's roles>)
OR
assigned_user_id = <user id>
```

**This second branch is what makes the QM workflow work without changing epms-api.** Because we pre-resolve `Visit.quality_approver_id` and pass it through as `assigned_user_id`, the QM user picks the task up via the personally-assigned branch — they don't need a `quality_manager` entry in their `all_roles` list.

## Findings

### F1: Status vocabulary mismatch 🔴 CRITICAL

**The problem.** [vms-api/app/models/visit.py](../vms-api/app/models/visit.py) declares `Visit.status` as a Postgres ENUM (`vms_visit_status` type) with values:

```
pending_approval, confirmed, checked_in, checked_out, cancelled, no_show
```

The approval engine, on `submit`, will write:

```python
doc.status = "submitted"
```

PostgreSQL will reject this with an enum violation, and the whole transaction rolls back. **Submitting any GMP visit fails.**

**Why SPRINT.md missed it.** S2-B line 300 says "`model=Visit, …, valid_* states from VisitStatus`" — it specified the *entry* states correctly, but didn't notice the engine then *writes* states from its own vocabulary.

**Fix — recommended option A: parallel `approval_status` column.**

```python
# In vms-api/app/models/visit.py — add ONE column.
approval_status: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
    String(20),
    nullable=True,
    server_default=None,
)
```

```python
# In approval-api/app/crud/engine.py — make engine read/write configurable.
# Tiny, backwards-compatible refactor: add status_attr to _DOC_META with default "status".

def _status_attr(meta: dict) -> str:
    return meta.get("status_attr", "status")

# Inside execute_action():
status_field = _status_attr(meta)
if getattr(doc, status_field) not in meta["valid_submit"]:
    raise ValueError(...)
setattr(doc, status_field, "submitted")
```

This is **a one-time tax across the engine** — about 20 line touches, all mechanical (`doc.status` → `getattr/setattr(doc, status_field, ...)`). Then the vms_visit entry in `_DOC_META` adds `"status_attr": "approval_status"` and our Visit's main `status: VisitStatus` is left alone.

**Why not option B (single field, free string).** Would force us to lose the `vms_visit_status` enum constraint at the DB layer, weakening every VMS read path.

**Why not option C (skip engine for vms_visit).** Loses auto-skip, ApprovalEvent log, dept-manager resolution, Portal Task Inbox integration. The point of S2-B is precisely to get those.

**Add a migration:**

```python
# vms-api/alembic/versions/20260601_0003_visit_approval_status.py
def upgrade() -> None:
    op.add_column("vms_visits",
                  sa.Column("approval_status", sa.String(20), nullable=True))
    # Optional: backfill historical visits with the user-facing status if it
    # happens to overlap (none currently do — leave NULL on existing rows).
```

---

### F2: `_actor_can_approve` signature needs `doc` 🟠 MAJOR

**The problem.** `_actor_can_approve` ([engine.py:237–264](../approval-api/app/crud/engine.py#L237-L264)) takes `creator_id` but not `doc`:

```python
async def _actor_can_approve(
    db, step_role, actor_id, actor_role, creator_id, rm, dept_gm_opm, finance_bp_ids,
) -> bool:
    ...
```

For `quality_manager`, we need to check `actor_id == doc.quality_approver_id`. No access to `doc`.

**Fix — add `doc` parameter:**

```python
async def _actor_can_approve(
    db, step_role, actor_id, actor_role, creator_id, rm, dept_gm_opm, finance_bp_ids,
    doc: Any | None = None,                     # NEW, keyword-only default for back-compat
) -> bool:
    if actor_role == "system_admin":
        return True
    ...
    if step_role == "quality_manager":
        if doc is None:
            return False
        expected = getattr(doc, "quality_approver_id", None)
        return expected is not None and actor_id == expected
    ...
```

And one caller in `execute_action()` at line 576 needs to pass `doc=doc`. Both changes together are ~10 lines.

---

### F3: `doc.title` missing from Visit 🟡 MINOR

**The problem.** Engine line 345 reads `doc.title`. Our Visit model has no `title` field.

**Fix — synthetic property on the approval-api Visit mirror:**

```python
# approval-api/app/models/visit.py — the mirror, NOT vms-api's full Visit model.
class Visit(UUIDPrimaryKey, Base):
    __tablename__ = "vms_visits"
    # ... only the fields the engine reads/writes ...
    visitor_id:          Mapped[uuid.UUID]
    host_id:             Mapped[uuid.UUID]
    created_by:          Mapped[uuid.UUID]
    access_area:         Mapped[str]
    approval_status:     Mapped[str | None]
    approval_step_idx:   Mapped[int | None]
    submitted_at:        Mapped[datetime | None]
    quality_approver_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None]

    @property
    def title(self) -> str:
        return f"GMP-zone visit {str(self.id)[:8]}"   # we don't have visitor name in this mirror

    @property
    def status(self):
        # Backwards-compat shim for any engine path that still reads `doc.status`
        # (we want them all to go through status_attr, but defensive belt+braces).
        return self.approval_status
```

**Better:** when we add the `approval_status` migration in F1, also add `visit_title` as a plain String(255) column populated by vms-api at submit time (`"VMS Visit — {visitor.first} {visitor.last} ({company})"`). Then the engine's title rendering gives auditors meaningful task titles in Portal without doing a join.

**Decision needed:** synthetic property (less data drift, weaker UX) vs real column (one extra string-write at submit time, much better task titles). **Recommend the real column.**

### F4: QM roster needed in W10 but scheduled in W11 🟠 MAJOR

**The problem.** S2-B (W10) `vms-api/app/services/approval.py` reads `vms_config.quality_manager_user_ids` to choose a QM and write it to `Visit.quality_approver_id` before calling approval-api. But the admin endpoints to *manage* that roster (`PUT /admin/quality-managers`) aren't built until S2-C (W11).

**Result.** W10 testing has nowhere to write the roster from. The only way to seed it during W10 is direct SQL.

**Fix.** Move the **backend** endpoints (just `GET` + `PUT /api/v1/admin/quality-managers` — ~40 lines + a Pydantic schema we already wrote in W2) up into W10's task list. The **frontend** Admin Panel UI stays in W11 as planned.

This is a pure SPRINT reordering — no architecture cost.

### F5: Portal Task Inbox already routes by `assigned_user_id` 🟢 WIN

**The discovery.** SPRINT W12 says Portal needs custom aggregation logic for `doc_type="vms_visit"`. But epms-api `task_crud.get_for_role` ([crud/task.py:142–173](../epms-api/app/crud/task.py#L142-L173)) already returns *all* tasks matching `assigned_user_id == me OR (assigned_user_id IS NULL AND assigned_role IN my_roles)`. So:

- For the `dept_manager` step → engine sets `assigned_user_id` via `_get_dept_manager_id` lookup → matches first branch. Already works.
- For the `quality_manager` step → engine sets `assigned_user_id` from `Visit.quality_approver_id` (our F2 special-case) → matches first branch. Already works.

**Portal-side cost reduces from "extend task aggregation" to "just register a deep-link path + label formatter":**

```diff
 // portal/src/pages/PortalHome.tsx
 const DOC_PATH: Record<string, string> = {
   pr: '/pr', po: '/po', pa: '/pa', gr: '/gr', invoice: '/invoices',
+  vms_visit: '/',           // VMS frontend visit detail is rooted at /
 }
 const STATUS_LABEL: Record<string, string> = {
   submitted: 'Pending Dept. Approval',
   ...
+  pending_approval: 'Pending Visit Approval',   // shared by VMS
 }
```

The deep-link href construction already handles arbitrary `doc_type` because it reads `DOC_PATH[t.document_type]`.

**Net:** SPRINT W12 Portal work drops from "~150 lines" to "~10 lines". Recover ~half a day from S2.

### F6: `tasks.document_type` is `String(10)` — 1 char of headroom 🟡 MINOR

**The problem.** [approval-api/app/models/task.py:18](../approval-api/app/models/task.py#L18):

```python
document_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(10), nullable=False)
```

`"vms_visit"` is 9 chars, fits. But:
- No room for a sub-type like `"vms_visit_priority"` or `"vms_audit"`.
- The next doc_type whoever adds (post-VMS) gets blocked by this column width.

**Fix.** Bump to `String(20)` via a migration:

```python
op.alter_column("tasks", "document_type", type_=sa.String(20))
```

This is unrelated to VMS — it's a tax we should pay opportunistically since we're touching approval-api anyway. Suggest **including in the W10 migration**.

### F7: Public-PC kiosk needs signed-URL subsystem (W9 scope creep) 🟠 MAJOR

**The problem.** SPRINT S2-A line 291:

> Public-PC self-fill mode: visitor can open `/visits/{id}/health-declaration` directly (no auth required for token URL — implement signed link with short expiry)

This is a non-trivial sub-feature:
- Short-lived signed-URL generator + verifier (~80 lines + tests)
- Public route (no JWT) on vms-api that accepts only signed URLs
- Frontend page that doesn't redirect to Portal on missing token
- Rate-limit / replay protection

That's 1–2 weeks of work hiding inside a one-line task.

**Recommendation:** Defer the kiosk path. For S2-A, ship only the **authenticated** Host-fills-in-on-behalf path:
- `POST /api/v1/visits/{id}/health-declaration` requires Host JWT
- VisitDetailPage's HealthDeclForm component does the actual signature capture
- Visitor signs on the Host's phone/tablet, not a public kiosk

The kiosk path goes into Phase 3 / out-of-sprint backlog. We can ship the GMP-gate compliance story without it.

### F9: No engine → VMS status handoff after approval 🟠 MAJOR

**The problem.** With F1's fix (parallel `approval_status` column), the engine writes `approval_status = "approved"`. But `Visit.status` is still `pending_approval`. The badge-print guard (W10 task: "if status==pending_approval → 422") will refuse to print until something flips `Visit.status → confirmed`.

PRD §6.2.1(3) step 6 said "approval-api updates `vms_visits.status` directly" — but with F1 it updates `approval_status`, not `status`.

**Fix.** Wire a post-approve callback in approval-api's `_POST_APPROVE` dict ([engine.py:491–501](../approval-api/app/crud/engine.py#L491-L501)):

```python
async def _post_approve_vms_visit(db: AsyncSession, visit: Visit) -> None:
    """Once fully approved, flip Visit.status from pending_approval to confirmed."""
    visit.status = "confirmed"   # the VMS enum string; we share the DB row, just a different column

_POST_APPROVE["vms_visit"] = _post_approve_vms_visit
```

And in `execute_action`'s rejection / return paths, vms-api needs to listen too. Cleanest: vms-api's `GET /api/v1/visits/{id}` reads the row and does this translation at read-time:

```python
# vms-api/app/crud/visit.py — read-time normalizer
def _sync_status_from_approval(visit: Visit) -> Visit:
    """If approval-api has written terminal state to approval_status, mirror it
    onto the user-facing status if vms-api hasn't already."""
    if visit.status != "pending_approval":
        return visit
    match visit.approval_status:
        case "approved": visit.status = "confirmed"
        case "rejected" | "cancelled": visit.status = "cancelled"
    return visit
```

This keeps the engine ignorant of the VMS enum and gives vms-api one centralized place to map between the two state spaces. (And — crucially — running this read-side doesn't depend on a webhook callback to vms-api, which the architecture explicitly avoids.)

## Recommended SPRINT changes

### Reorder W10 / W11

**Move into W10 (S2-B):**
- approval-api: `_DOC_META["vms_visit"]` + `_WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS["vms_visit"]` + `_DOC_TYPES` extension
- approval-api: `Visit` mirror model + `_post_approve_vms_visit` callback (F9)
- approval-api: `status_attr` refactor (F1) + `_actor_can_approve(doc)` signature (F2) + `tasks.document_type` widen to 20 chars (F6)
- vms-api: `0003` migration — add `approval_status: String(20)` + `visit_title: String(255)` (F1 + F3)
- vms-api: `/api/v1/admin/quality-managers` GET/PUT (backend only) (F4)
- vms-api: read-side status sync helper (F9)
- vms-api: `services/approval.py` — picks a QM, writes `quality_approver_id` + `visit_title`, calls engine submit
- vms-api: print-badge guard for `status==pending_approval`
- vms-api: cancel cascades to engine `cancel`

**Move into W11 (S2-C):**
- All Admin Panel UI (QM roster page, notification contacts page, etc.)
- Portal Task Inbox `DOC_PATH` / `STATUS_LABEL` extension (the 10-line tweak from F5)
- Portal Admin → Workflow Defs editor: add VMS Visit tab

**S2-A (W9):** Scope down per F7 — authenticated Host flow only; defer kiosk to backlog.

**S2-E (W11/12):** Unblock with Compliance now per F8; ship generic exporter as fallback.

### Net effort estimate

| Sprint | SPRINT.md hours | Reality after this review |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| S2-A (W9)  | ~40 | ~25 (kiosk deferred) |
| S2-B (W10) | ~40 | ~55 (status mirror + signature changes + QM endpoints pulled in) |
| S2-C (W11) | ~40 | ~35 (Portal task inbox simpler, just UI work) |
| S2-D (W12) | ~30 | ~15 (Portal almost free per F5) |
| S2-E (W11–12) | ~40 | ~20 (skeleton exporter; rebuild after Compliance) |
| **Total** | **~190** | **~150** |

Net: small savings + much lower technical risk, **but the savings only materialize if F1 + F2 + F9 land cleanly in W10**. If W10 slips, the rest of S2 stacks behind it.

| 6 | F8: CFIA format — wait for Compliance or interim? | ✅ **Use an interim sample format.** Ship S2-E generic exporter against a temporary column list that approximates CFIA; mark as "interim, pending Compliance review" in UI. Compliance can hand-edit final format after seeing real output. |
| 7 | QM round-robin vs first-active strategy (W10)? | ✅ **First-active.** `pick_quality_manager()` returns `cfg.quality_manager_user_ids[0]` (first entry whose user is still active). Round-robin remains a Phase 3 enhancement gated by QA team request. |

All 7 are settled — W9 / W10 implementation can quote this section as the source of truth.

## Code sketches (drop-in for W10)

### 1. approval-api: new Visit mirror

```python
# approval-api/app/models/visit.py  (NEW FILE)
"""Read-write mirror of vms_visits for the approval engine.

vms-api owns the full Visit model (with the VisitStatus enum). This mirror
exposes ONLY the columns the engine reads/writes — same DB row, narrower view.
"""
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

from sqlalchemy import DateTime, ForeignKey, Integer, String
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.db.base import Base, UUIDPrimaryKey


class Visit(UUIDPrimaryKey, Base):
    __tablename__ = "vms_visits"

    # Owned by vms-api — we just read.
    visitor_id:  Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(UUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=False)
    host_id:     Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(UUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=False)
    created_by:  Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(UUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=False)
    access_area: Mapped[str]       = mapped_column(String(40), nullable=False)
    visit_title: Mapped[str]       = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=False)  # NEW in 0003
    quality_approver_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="RESTRICT"),
        nullable=True,
    )

    # Owned by approval-api — we read AND write.
    approval_status:   Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(20), nullable=True)   # NEW in 0003
    approval_step_idx: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=True)
    submitted_at:      Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)

    # Engine reads `doc.title` directly (engine.py:345).
    @property
    def title(self) -> str:
        return self.visit_title
```

### 3. approval-api: status_attr indirection (F1)

```python
# approval-api/app/crud/engine.py — replace status reads/writes in execute_action.
def _status_of(meta: dict, doc) -> str:
    return getattr(doc, meta.get("status_attr", "status"))

def _set_status(meta: dict, doc, value: str) -> None:
    setattr(doc, meta.get("status_attr", "status"), value)

# Inside execute_action():
if act == "submit":
    if _status_of(meta, doc) not in meta["valid_submit"]:
        raise ValueError(...)
    _set_status(meta, doc, "submitted")
    ...
elif act == "approve":
    if _status_of(meta, doc) not in meta["valid_approve"]:
        raise ValueError(...)
    ...
    if next_step < len(workflow):
        _set_status(meta, doc, "in_review")
    else:
        _set_status(meta, doc, "approved")
        ...
# (similar for return / reject / recall / cancel / process)
```

# approval-api/app/crud/engine.py

async def _create_approve_task(db, doc_type, doc, step, workflow, meta, rm, dept_gm_opm):
    wf = workflow[step]
    role = wf["role"]
    assigned_user_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
    assigned_role = role

    if role == "dept_manager":
        assigned_user_id = await _get_dept_manager_id(db, doc.created_by)
    elif role == "gm_or_opm":
        assigned_role, assigned_user_id = await _resolve_gm_or_opm(db, doc.created_by, rm, dept_gm_opm)
    elif role == "quality_manager" and doc_type == "vms_visit":
        # F2: VMS-local. vms-api pre-selected the QM and stored on the visit.
        assigned_user_id = getattr(doc, "quality_approver_id", None)
    ...


async def _actor_can_approve(

    if step_role == "quality_manager":
        if doc is None:
            return False
        expected = getattr(doc, "quality_approver_id", None)
        return expected is not None and actor_id == expected

### 5. approval-api: post-approve callback (F9)

```python
async def _post_approve_vms_visit(db: AsyncSession, visit: VmsVisit) -> None:
    """After all approval steps pass, hand control back to vms-api by flipping
    Visit.status (the user-facing VisitStatus enum) from pending_approval → confirmed.

    vms-api will see this on next read; no callback HTTP request needed.
    """
    # Use raw SQL update because we're touching a column not in the mirror.
    await db.execute(
        text("UPDATE vms_visits SET status = 'confirmed' WHERE id = :id"),
        {"id": visit.id},
    )

_POST_APPROVE["vms_visit"] = _post_approve_vms_visit
```

### 6. vms-api: submit helper

```python
# vms-api/app/services/approval.py (NEW)
"""Bridge between vms-api business logic and approval-api engine.

Decides per-visit whether to invoke approval-api at all (based on access_area),
resolves the Quality Manager candidate (for GMP/Lab visits), and calls the
engine's submit action. The actual state machine lives in approval-api.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import random
import uuid

import httpx

from app.core.config import settings
from app.models.visit import AccessArea, Visit, VisitStatus
from app.models.vms_config import VmsConfig

_NEEDS_APPROVAL = frozenset({
    AccessArea.warehouse,
    AccessArea.production_non_gmp,
    AccessArea.production_gmp,
    AccessArea.laboratory,
    AccessArea.all,
})
_NEEDS_QUALITY_MANAGER = frozenset({
    AccessArea.production_gmp,
    AccessArea.laboratory,
    AccessArea.all,
})


def access_requires_approval(area: AccessArea) -> bool:
    return area in _NEEDS_APPROVAL


def access_requires_quality_manager(area: AccessArea) -> bool:
    return area in _NEEDS_QUALITY_MANAGER


def pick_quality_manager(cfg: VmsConfig) -> uuid.UUID | None:
    """First-active strategy for MVP. PRD §11.4 #8 leaves round-robin open."""
    ids = cfg.quality_manager_user_ids or []
    if not ids:
        return None
    # uuid.UUID() roundtrip in case JSONB returns strings
    return uuid.UUID(ids[0])


async def submit_for_approval(
    visit: Visit, bearer_token: str, *, visitor_label: str,
) -> dict:
    """Set draft+title fields then POST submit to approval-api.

    Caller must commit the SQLAlchemy session AFTER this returns successfully
    so the row vms-api wrote (approval_status='draft', visit_title=…) is visible
    to approval-api's own session that reads from the same DB.
    """
    visit.visit_title = visitor_label[:255]
    visit.approval_status = "draft"
    visit.status = VisitStatus.pending_approval
    # NOTE: caller is responsible for db.flush() / commit before the POST below.

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10) as client:
        resp = await client.post(
            f"{settings.APPROVAL_ENGINE_URL}/approvals/vms_visit/{visit.id}/action",
            json={"action": "submit"},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {bearer_token}"},
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.json()
```

### 7. vms-api: read-side status sync (F9)

```python
# vms-api/app/crud/visit.py — small helper called from get_visit / list_visits.

def sync_status_from_approval(visit: Visit) -> Visit:
    """Translate engine-state writes back into the VMS-facing VisitStatus.

    Engine writes to `approval_status` (F1). When it reaches a terminal state
    we mirror it onto the user-facing `status` enum so the rest of vms-api
    (badge guards, dashboard counters, etc.) doesn't have to know about the
    parallel field.

    Safe to call on every read — only flips when there's something to flip.
    """
    if visit.status != VisitStatus.pending_approval:
        return visit
    match visit.approval_status:
        case "approved":
            visit.status = VisitStatus.confirmed
        case "rejected" | "cancelled":
            visit.status = VisitStatus.cancelled
    return visit
```

## What this review is NOT

- Not a re-litigation of the PRD V2.3 architectural choice "use approval-api via cfm-style integration". That decision stands. The above only fills in details that were under-specified.
- Not a defense of the existing engine design. (`status: String` with hardcoded vocabulary is debt; we work with it.)
- Not exhaustive on S3 — Phase 3 work isn't reviewed here.
